title: The Morning After Micron, Jobs Tomorrow, Iran LACKS Progress.
speaker: Kevin Paffrath

macro_themes.view: Thinks the 10y yield rise is driven mainly by Japanese investors repatriating out of US Treasuries; called the yield peak near 5.27% and expects yields down once that and the Iran war end.
90-95% confident of a US-Iran deal by the midterm election; Trump is deliberately waiting for a better deal, so volatility may last ~3 weeks.
Challenger job cuts down, S&P and ISM manufacturing PMIs in expansion; mid-cycle boom, though ISM prices paid show inflation pressure.
The 10s-2s spread approaching ~50bp historically means something breaks; 16 of 16 similar yield runs broke something.
Rising H100/H200 rental prices and GPU hardware values show the AI buildout is not rolling over; it is a bubble but still money to be made.

calls.condition: Bullish once Japanese repatriation fades and an Iran deal is struck; volatility possible for ~3 weeks before that
calls.reason: Strong economic data, loose credit and rising GPU values; only the 10y yield is the problem, which he expects to fade with an Iran deal and end of Japanese selling.
calls.quote: by the end of the year, we'll probably not only have record highs on the Q's, but the NASDAQ 100 will probably exceed

calls.condition: Conditional on Iran deal and end of Japanese Treasury selling
calls.reason: Earnings growth vs valuation compression sets up a euphoric boom after midterms; November/December expected to be strong.
calls.quote: Stock markets got a boom into Q4. I mean, November, December should be freaking glorious.

calls.condition: Yields fall once Japanese repatriation stops and Iran war ends; Japanese dumping could still push yields higher short term
calls.reason: Called peak yields at 5.27; currently 5.31-5.32. Attributes the rise to Japan selling Treasuries (record ~$80B reserve drop) and BOJ/Fed spread rather than US fundamentals.
calls.quote: 5.27 is when I called the 10-year Treasury as we are pretty damn close to peak.

calls.condition: If an Iran deal is struck
calls.reason: Brent has come off the 107-109 highs to ~100; expects further decline on an Iran deal.
calls.quote: We've got oil declining back to $100. And honestly, it's probably once we get an Iran deal, it's going to go even lower.

calls.reason: Trades ~29.8x forward EPS with ~45% forecast growth (PEG ~0.64) and ~54% net margins; argues a 2.7 PEG on 11.67 EPS implies ~$1,400.
calls.quote: You know this could be a $1,400 stock. So that's insane to think about but it shows you how cheap this dog is right now.

calls.reason: Earnings growth expected to turn negative and DRAM pricing compression lowers terminal growth; intraday test of holding above -2% failed (stock down ~3%).
calls.quote: It's why I haven't been super jazzed about Micron.

calls.reason: Calls the rebound a probable dead-cat bounce; says Broadcom is cheaper on PEG with better margins, so prefers AVGO over the FICO dip.
calls.quote: FICO's got its probable deadcat bounce.

notes: Date: morning after Micron earnings, PMI report dated 10/1/26, 'Happy October', jobs report 'tomorrow'. QQQ quoted as 'NASDAQ 100' (735, dip buys 700-715, 800 target are QQQ levels). Micron level 1019 garbled/unclear. Also passing mentions: SpaceX up 1% (holder), Opendoor ~2.30 (thought bottom near 2.50, not a buyer), XLF rolling over; not recorded. 'Still holding 227' likely NVDA level.
